title: Research data forensics
subtitle: I rebuild and prove a research dataset before I trust it.

stats.label: golden examples rebuilt from two sources

lede: Research and inventions mentions the curated corpus of golden examples from my first distillation pipeline. When I came back to it, the corpus was split between a PostgreSQL database that had kept changing and a SQLite backup. Neither was complete, and no notes said how its cluster centroids had been computed. I decided to rebuild it from both sources and reproduce its derived data exactly before trusting any of it. I directed the recovery in phases, each closed by a written report. I treated the database and the backup as two independent witnesses: they were compared entry by entry, every gap in one was explained from the other, and each filled the other's gaps.
quote: Two views of the same data that disagree mislead every model trained on them.
evidence: Data recovery and forensics: a corpus of about 12,000 golden examples rebuilt from a changing PostgreSQL database and a 13 GB SQLite backup, compared entry by entry.
Reproducible data pipelines: the centroid computation reverse-engineered from the stored centroids, so recovered data is derived the same way as the original.
ML data quality: alignment measured between passage medoids and mean question-and-answer embeddings, with phantom clusters that had no source text set aside.
author: Corey James
